And when its masters prepared to fight,
Saladin did not wish to fight against it,
but set an army against it,
and commanded that they should prevent its people from going out and entering.
And when they were hard-pressed,
they surrendered it quickly.
And Saladin came against Mosul,
and surrounded it with an army from all sides.
Now Izz al-Din, its master, sent to the Caliph,
and asked of him to intercede on his behalf with Saladin.
And the Caliph sent an envoy to him and interceded with him;
but he demanded that the people of Mosul should give him the gold he had spent on his coming,
or that they should give him Aleppo.
The people of Mosul, however, replied,
"We have no gold,
and Aleppo has another master,
Imad al-Din;
how can we give you a land that is not ours?" And when Saladin saw that he was unable to subdue it,
he left it and went to Sinjar,
and waged war against it,
and took it from Sharaf al-Din, son of Qutb al-Din Mawdud.
And from there Saladin went against the city of Dara,
and its master, Samsam al-Din Bahram, of the Artuqids, came out to serve him,
and showed humility and submission,
and he left his city to him.
And he went to Harran,
and dismissed his armies so that each man might go to his own country and rest in his house,
because it was the winter season,
and it was the days of the fast and festival of the Arabs (Muslims);
and he himself remained with a few men in Harran.
Then the people of Mosul,
fearing lest in the spring he should return against them and take Mosul as he had taken Sinjar {OCR?},
sent to Shah-Armen, the lord of Khilat,
and asked help from him.
And that Shah-Armen gladly answered their request,
and sent to his sister's son, Qutb al-Din Ilghazi, son of Alpi, son of Timurtash, the master of Mardin, the maternal uncle of Izz al-Din, the master of Mosul.
And all the Mardinites, the Mosulites, and the men of Shah-Armen assembled at Harzem {OCR?};
and there also came to them one thousand seven hundred Yaruqid horsemen from Aleppo,
and they prepared to fight with Saladin.
When he heard that his enemies had assembled,
he was shaken and trembling seized him;
and he sent in haste for his armies to gather to him.
And within eight days they were all with him,
